newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares rebound, seen watching U.S. rates.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares rebound, seen watching U.S. rates.

text.p: Polish shares on Monday rebounded after falling most of last week and analysts said that after a possible rise on Tuesday all eyes would be on the U.S. Federal Reserve's Federal Open Market Committee meeting.

They said Monday's stronger buying after price-fixing and mixed continuous trade gave hope for a Tuesday gain but that the possible 25-basis-point interest-rate rise at the FOMC meeting could lead to falls on Wednesday.
"A rate rise should have a negative psychological effect, though merit-wise it may have already been discounted," said Emil Onyszczuk of Polish Development Bank (PBR) brokerage.

The main market's all-share WIG index rose 1.4 percent to 16,192.2 points and turnover fell 20.7 percent to 127.2 million zlotys ($41.3 million) on all three markets. Gainers led losers by 68 to 10 with 15 stocks stable.
Before the session the main market had fallen 12.9 percent since its February 18 three-year high.
Analysts said the market could find support above 15,500.
They were cheered by Monday rises by large-cap Bank Slaski and tyremaker Stomil Olsztyn after recent falls.

Both rose at or above four percent while steel trader Stalexport gained 5.7 percent in active trade, helping the large-cap WIG 20 index end the regular session equal with the overall market's 1.4-percent rise.
Analysts said top gainer Espebepe jumped 8.1 percent as speculators continued to play on the uncertain future of the construction firm which faces possible bankruptcy.
Mass privatisation NFI units rose 1.6 percent in regular trade and were flat in continuous trade, where stocks were mixed and the WIG 20 index rose 0.6 percent.
